title: Prevent a package from updating
summary: Use apt-mark to hold a package at its current version. This stops the package manager from upgrading it, which is useful if a new version breaks your software.
prerequisites: Know the exact name of the package you want to hold.

steps.explain: Mark the package as 'held' so apt will not upgrade it.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: The name of the package to hold.

alternatives.explain: Puts an installed package on hold to prevent it from being automatically upgraded.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: The name of the installed package to hold

verify.expect: The package name appears in the list.

rollback.explain: Remove the hold to allow the package to update again.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: The name of the package to unhold.

warnings: Holding a package prevents security updates for that specific package. Only hold packages if you have a specific reason.
